title: At the Travel Agency
description: The lesson where a holiday goes wrong and language has to repair it: the words of the counter (to book, a reservation, a deposit, the balance, a refund, a discount, a voucher, a package holiday, a transfer, an excursion, airport taxes, facilities, scheduled, superb, disappointed, an oil refinery), what "included" really covers in the small print of a booking and why a deposit is not a refund, the ladder of dissatisfaction from "not quite what we expected" to "far from satisfactory" with the British understatement that hides a strong complaint under a mild sentence, the four moves of a complaint - open it, state what happened, recall the promise that was broken, say what you want - firmly and politely, in speech at the desk and in a letter to the manager, asking for compensation that matches what was lost, and above all the reported speech that carries the broken promise: "You'll be met at the airport" becoming "You said that we would be met at the airport, but nobody came", with the backshift of will into would and of the present into the past, the advertisement's you turning into we while the new you names the person who made the promise, the reporting verbs that give a complaint its force (complain, add, point out, promise), the duty to report faithfully what was really said, and the reverse reading that recovers the original words from a report; plus the agent's reply - apologise, explain, refuse, offer compensation - and word stress on the lesson's own vocabulary, from PACKage and SCHEDule to dePOSit, reFINery and disapPOINTed
sources: Official programme transcript - content/programmes-officiels/programme/bac-math/anglais.md, Unit 1 UNIT OUTLINE (p. 36) and Unit 1 lesson 7 "At the Travel Agency" (p. 68-73): listening to a conversation, expressing dissatisfaction, complaining, reported speech, word stress
